topStories.headline: OSU Marion Opens Downtown Engagement Hub on North Main Street
topStories.dek: Ohio State University at Marion has cut the ribbon on a new community space at 146 N. Main Street, giving faculty, students, and residents a shared downtown home for collaboration.
topStories.body:
The Ohio State University at Marion opened its Downtown Engagement Hub on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, with a ribbon-cutting ceremony held from 4 to 6 p.m. at 146 N. Main Street — a building that has, over the years, been a restaurant, a pawn shop, and various other businesses. The university says the Hub is not intended to function as a classroom or satellite office but rather as a place where people who live and work in Marion and those who teach and study at Ohio State can sit down together and build something.

Dean and Director Jennifer Schlueter spoke with WOSU Public Media ahead of the opening, describing the Hub's aim to bring people together to collaborate and work on solutions for the community. The space is designed to host design-thinking sessions, civic roundtables, public exhibits, student showcases, leadership workshops, and cultural programming — with an explicit goal of connecting the campus more directly to downtown Marion's ongoing revival.

The Hub also provides a physical home for the recently launched Marion Futures Lab, a one-year community project supported by a $49,480 Community Engagement seed grant from Ohio State. Led by Professor of Psychology Dr. Nikole Patson, the Futures Lab brings together faculty, students, artists, and community members to explore how shared memories and cultural traditions shape Marion's future, with plans for public events, performances, exhibitions, and a digital Marion Memories Atlas.

Faculty wishing to hold community office hours downtown, run class sessions, or place community-engaged research projects are encouraged to reach out to Leslie Beyer-Hermsen at the Hub. Members of the public can walk in off the street.

topStories.headline: Marion City Schools Holds 3-Star State Report Card Rating for Second Year Running
topStories.dek: The district's 2025–26 Ohio State Report Card shows continued momentum in graduation rates and career readiness, with Harding High School and Garfield Elementary leading gains.
topStories.body:
Marion City Schools sustained its overall 3-Star rating on the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce's 2025–26 State Report Card for the second consecutive year, with notable gains in two specific categories. Both Graduation Rate and College, Career, Workforce and Military Readiness climbed from 2 Stars to 3 Stars, according to reporting by Marion County Now. Harding High School and Garfield Elementary led the district's strongest improvements.

The results build on momentum the district highlighted at the start of the school year. Superintendent Brian Murphy's annual State of Our Schools address had pointed to $1.9 million dedicated to strengthening K–12 literacy instruction and new curriculum maps as drivers of the progress. The district's stated theme for the 2025–26 year is 'Achieve. Believe. Connect.'

Marion City Schools serves students across the city, with Marion Harding High School as the district's sole high school.

topStories.headline: Judge Disqualifies Prosecutor from Marion Police Officer's Rape Case
topStories.dek: Marion County Common Pleas Court Judge Matthew Frericks has ruled that Prosecutor Ray Grogan cannot prosecute the case against officer Brendon Damron, citing conflict-of-interest concerns.
topStories.body:
Marion County Common Pleas Court Judge Matthew Frericks issued a decision this week disqualifying Marion County Prosecutor Ray Grogan from prosecuting the criminal case involving Marion Police Officer Brendon Damron, according to Marion County Now. The ruling is the latest development in a high-profile case that has wound through multiple conflict-of-interest challenges since Damron's arrest in February.

Damron, 24, is facing two counts of rape and one count of abduction stemming from an alleged off-duty incident reported to have occurred at a private residence on February 11. He was taken into custody on February 13 and has been on leave from the Marion Police Department. Earlier in the case, the Ohio Supreme Court separately disqualified Marion County Common Pleas Judge Todd Anderson from presiding over the trial, with Chief Justice Sharon L. Kennedy ruling that the disqualification was necessary to preserve the fairness and integrity of the judicial process.

Defense attorney Joel Spitzer had argued that intertwined professional ties between the Marion Police Department, the Sheriff's Office, and the Prosecutor's Office created conflicts of interest. With Judge Frericks's latest ruling removing Grogan from the prosecution, the case will require a different office to take over. Marion County Now has indicated it will continue to cover the developing story.
